correctness.rationale: The weak-2-summability constraint is exactly sum_j u_j u_j^T <= I. For u_e=(L^dagger)^(1/2)b_e, their covariance frame sum is QLQ=P_(1^perp), proving admissibility and the lower bound from the e-th output coordinate. Since sum_e rho_e=tr(QL)=tr L^(1/2), scalar Cauchy–Schwarz forces baseline S/sqrt(m), with equality iff all rho_e constant. For any edge, spectral Cauchy–Schwarz |b_e^Tu|² <= rho_e u^T L^(1/2)u, then the matrix trace constraint gives pi_2² <= (max rho_e) S. Hence constant rho_e makes both bounds coincide, and converse follows from the lower bound. For strongly regular graphs, Q belongs to the adjacency Bose–Mesner algebra span{I,A,J}, so rho_e is constant even when edge transitivity fails. Independently checked exact matrix identities and numerical eigenvalue bounds for all 38 connected labelled four-vertex graphs, including 30 nonuniform and 8 uniform-rho cases, and reconstructed stated cyclic/complete spectral formulas.
residual_risks: No exact pi_2 formula for graphs with nonconstant rho_e is asserted; finite numeric graph sweep corroborates, not proves, the spectral inequality.
